title: Palindrome Linked List
prompt:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, determine whether the list reads the same forward and backward (i.e. whether it is a palindrome).

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,2,2,1]` represents `1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, check the palindrome property by manipulating the nodes (not just the original array), and return `True` or `False`.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 5 * 10^4]
hints: Copying the values into an array and checking that array is a palindrome works, but can you do it with O(1) extra space?
Use slow/fast pointers to find the middle of the list, then reverse the second half in place.
Once the second half is reversed, walk it alongside the first half and compare values node by node — they should match all the way through.

solution.approach: Find the middle of the list with slow/fast pointers. Reverse the second half in place. Then walk the first half and the reversed second half together, comparing values at each step; if any pair differs, it's not a palindrome. Because the second half is reversed and the two pointers advance together, if the whole list is a palindrome every comparison must succeed until one half runs out.
